items.title: Redesign Smart Money dashboard page: Winning Whales leaderboard + readable whale activity
items.action: User feedback: the old dashboard/pages/4_Smart_Money.py page was not clear about what the most recent trades were, raw Kalshi tickers were unreadable, and there was no way to see or act on which wallets were actually winning. Investigated: sources.accounts.diagnose_discovery() only ever surfaced aggregate funnel COUNTS, never the actual vetted wallet list -- discover_winners()'s real per-wallet data (address, display_name, win_rate, resolved_count, resolved_cash_pnl, and each wallet's current active_markets with title/outcome/pct_pnl/url) was already computed and persisted to data/winning_accounts.json by the live daily pipeline, but had zero UI anywhere on this page. Separately, the whale-activity (streak) table showed a bare ticker column with no way to build a real Kalshi link (streak.json only ever stored the raw ticker) and no way to sort by recency (only by streak length).
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-31. Full page redesign: (1) NEW 'Winning Whales' panel, now first on the page -- reads a new sources.accounts.read_cached_winners() (pure read-only peek at winning_accounts.json, deliberately never triggers a live discover_winners() crawl, unlike load_winners()) and renders a wallet leaderboard (win rate, resolved count, cash P&L, clickable Polymarket profile link) plus a 'Live Picks' feed: every winning wallet's current open position, market title, side, conviction %, and a clickable link, sorted by conviction descending -- the literal actionable output the user asked for. Handles the real current state (0 winning wallets qualify right now) with an honest empty-state message pointing at the funnel diagnostic, not a broken-looking blank page. (2) The existing Wallet Discovery Funnel panel is kept but reframed as supporting 'why' context for panel 1, moved second. (3) Whale Activity (renamed from 'Whale Streak Leaderboard' to disambiguate from panel 1 -- explicit new page-level caption distinguishes 'proven track record' from 'no track record, just big size') gets a new core.logger.get_market_meta_for_tickers() (resolves series_ticker/event_ticker, not just title) so every row gets a real clickable Kalshi link instead of a bare ticker, plus a 'Most recent / Longest streak' sort toggle. Since core/kalshi.py unconditionally imports the kalshi-sdk package (not installed in the dashboard's actual Python environment -- streamlit isn't in the project's own venv either), the tiny confirmed kalshi_market_url() URL-format logic is deliberately duplicated inline in the dashboard page rather than imported, avoiding a real import crash. 2 new logger tests, 3 new accounts tests, full suite green (2309 passed). Verified via Streamlit's AppTest harness against both real live data (0 winners, correctly shows the honest empty state; 101 real whale-activity rows render with working links/titles) and synthetic populated winner data (to exercise the leaderboard/live-picks tables, which real data can't currently cover) -- both clean, no exceptions, interactive sort/slider controls exercised successfully.

items.title: Dashboard-wide caption/help-text accuracy passthrough + fix broken Signal Breakdown click-filter
items.action: User feedback after the Smart Money redesign (smart-money-winning-whales-panel): a direct question ("so the streak on the table is associated with a wallet correct?") caught a real inaccuracy in my own dashboard captions (whale-activity streak wrongly implied wallet/trader identity, when core/whales.py has zero wallet concept -- Kalshi order book exposes size/direction only, never who placed a trade). User then asked for the same code-verified passthrough on every other dashboard page. Findings, each cross-checked against actual code/live data, not assumed: (1) dashboard/app.py -- Median Edge KPI help text implied a signed/directional meaning for `edge`, but core/scorer.py designs edge as an unsigned magnitude (direction is a separate field) and live data/powerbi_export/signals.csv had genuine negative edge values (6/37 non-null) since the primary scoring path lets Claude self-report edge without server-side abs() enforcement -- caption rewritten, forced +sign removed from the number format. (2) dashboard/pages/2_Signal_Breakdown.py -- a stale hardcoded "13/46" resolved-count figure in the CLV-drift empty-state message, now computed live from the current signals DataFrame instead. (3) dashboard/pages/3_Signal_Log.py -- same wallet/identity-conflation pattern as the whale-streak fix, in the whale_detected KPI help text ("a big bettor... someone with information is confident") -- reworded to state plainly there is no identity behind the signal. (4) dashboard/pages/5_Backlog.py -- reviewed against backlog/checker.py's actual functions, no inaccuracies found. Separately, while running AppTest against 2_Signal_Breakdown.py for the first time this session (previous verification only read the file, never executed it), found a REAL production bug unrelated to wording: st.plotly_chart(..., on_select="rerun") requires Streamlit >=1.35, but the dashboard's actually-deployed environment (anaconda python, confirmed via streamlit.__version__) pins 1.30.0, where on_select/selection_mode/key are silently swallowed by plotly_chart's **kwargs and the call always returns a plain DeltaGenerator, not a selection-state dict -- so the click-to-filter chart crashed the entire page on every load with real flag_path data (i.e. always). Fixed by guarding with isinstance(event, dict) so the feature no-ops safely on 1.30.0 and will light back up automatically if Streamlit is ever upgraded. Also fixed the matching false claim in dashboard/README.md ("confirmed present in the pinned Streamlit version's signature") and a second stale hardcoded count ("13-16 resolved bets", actual live count 25/54) in the same file.
items.notes: Verified: all 5 dashboard files (app.py, pages/2-5) syntax-checked via ast.parse; app.py and pages 2_Signal_Breakdown.py/3_Signal_Log.py re-run via streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest (timeout=150) with zero exceptions both before and after the plotly_chart fix; full test suite (tests/, anaconda python for AppTest, project python for pytest) 2309 passed / 1 skipped, no regressions. items.title: runs.model_used read a cosmetic config key, not the real --model flag actually used
items.action: Found 2026-09-01 while checking the first Opus-trial run's result row: run_meta['model_used'] (main.py:246) read config.scoring.scorer_model -- a static, cosmetic-only field never passed to any actual API/CLI call (per core/scorer.py's own docstring) -- completely disconnected from config.llm.cli_model_override (wire-llm-model-cli-flag, done 2026-08-31), the key that actually controls which model scores markets on the live cli backend. Concretely: after flipping cli_model_override to 'opus' and running main.py, the resulting runs table row still said model_used='claude-sonnet-4-6', wrongly implying Sonnet had scored it. Verified via code-path analysis (main.load_config() resolves the override correctly, and score_markets() at main.py:860 passes the same unmodified config through to core.scorer, which appends --model when set) that Opus was actually used for that run despite the mislabeled field -- this was a reporting bug, not a wiring failure of the trial itself.
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-01. main.py:246 now prefers config.llm.cli_model_override when backend='cli' and it's set, falling back to the original scoring.scorer_model cosmetic default otherwise -- so today's behavior when no override is set is unchanged. Full suite green (2309 passed, 1 skipped) after the change; no dedicated unit test added since main.py's orchestration has no test harness by design (verified via direct load_config()+logic re-derivation instead, same precedent as other main.py-only fixes this project). Trial run 1's own DB row (run_id 865ba8a5, 2026-09-01T22:09:26Z) still shows the stale label since it predates this fix -- left as-is rather than retroactively rewritten, with this note as the record of why it's actually Opus despite what the row says. All future trial runs (including this fix's own commit) will self-report correctly.

items.title: resolve_first.py's log_selected() never carried category into logged signals
items.action: User feedback: dashboard/live category diversity felt low. Investigated live (not assumed): signals.category cross-tabulated by flag_path showed DRIFT/HEURISTIC (main.py's Claude-scored paths) have real diversity -- 11 distinct Kalshi categories -- but every single RESOLVE_FIRST row (39/39) was blank, 100%. Traced the full data path: the snapshot file resolve_first.py reads (data/snapshots/markets_*.json) has category populated on all 3037 markets (confirmed live), so the source data was never the problem -- this is a DIFFERENT, later-stage gap than signal-category-mostly-blank-despite-real-data (2026-08-26, already fixed main.py's fallback path and attach_event_category_metadata's silent-swallow logging). Root cause: analysis/resolve_first.py's log_selected() builds its own signal dict from the source market dict field-by-field (ticker/title/event_ticker/series_ticker/etc.) and simply never included category in that list -- the same class of 'computed/available but never carried into the output dict' gap already found twice elsewhere this session (Smart Money's pick view model, the subscriber report's whale fields). Separately confirmed via the full live snapshot (not just the signals table) that Kalshi's real taxonomy has 15 categories total (Elections, Economics, Sports, Politics, Crypto, Entertainment, Commodities, Financials, Companies, Science and Technology, Climate and Weather, Social, Health, World, Transportation) -- category is already sourced directly and exclusively from Kalshi's own field with no synthetic taxonomy or whitelist anywhere in the codebase, so 'match how Kalshi labels them' was already true by construction. The 4 categories missing from signals.category (Social, Health, World, Transportation) are just thin market slices (19/10/7/1 open markets respectively) that haven't produced a flagged signal yet, not a code gap -- no fix needed or possible there short of waiting for real signal volume.
items.notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-01. Added `"category": m.get("category", ""),` to log_selected()'s signal dict (analysis/resolve_first.py). 2 new tests (test_category_stored, test_category_blank_when_absent -- never fabricates a category the source market lacks) added to tests/test_resolve_first.py, 29/29 passing. This only affects NEW resolve_first signals going forward -- the existing 39 blank RESOLVE_FIRST rows stay blank (same Kalshi-404-on-expired-events unbackfillable-history constraint as the original 2026-08-26 fix, unrelated to this specific gap since these are still-open near-dated markets in most cases, but retroactively rewriting already-logged rows from inference rather than a real historical fetch is not this fix's job).
